question_text: On a government survey map, the scale is 1:50,000. If two barangays are 8 cm apart on the map, what is the actual distance in kilometers?

hint_ladder.title: Scale 1:50,000: What It Means
hint_ladder.text: Kapag sinabing 1:50,000, ibig sabihin 1 cm sa mapa = 50,000 cm sa totoong mundo. Same unit pa rin—centimeter muna.

hint_ladder.title: Multiply Lang, Kuha Mo!
hint_ladder.text: 8 cm sa mapa? Multiply mo sa 50,000: 8 × 50,000 = 400,000 cm real distance. Simple arithmetic lang, huwag malito.

hint_ladder.title: Kilometer Conversion: 100,000 cm = 1 km
hint_ladder.text: Dito madami nalilito. Tandaan: 100 cm = 1 m, 1,000 m = 1 km, so 100 × 1,000 = 100,000 cm per km. Yakagin: “centi‑kilo, 100k ang sagot!”

hint_ladder.title: Final Division: 400,000 ÷ 100,000
hint_ladder.text: 400,000 cm ÷ 100,000 cm/km = 4 km. Kung lumitaw na 2, 3, o 5, check conversion mo. 4 km ang tamang sagot.

A.text: You might have chosen A because you divided by 200,000 instead of 100,000, or forgot to multiply by 50,000 entirely.

B.text: You might have chosen B because you used an incorrect conversion like dividing by 133,333.

D.text: You might have chosen D because you divided by 80,000 instead of 100,000, a common unit slip.

next_time_rule: Real cm = map cm × scale; then ÷100,000 for km (kasi 100 cm/m × 1,000 m/km). Tandaan ang 100k rule para iwas mali!
deconstruct_text:
Imagine you're a barangay secretary plotting the distance between the daycare center and the health center on a map of Candon. The scale is 1:50,000, and the map shows 8 cm. So, 1 cm sa mapa = 50,000 cm sa lupa. Multiply 8 × 50,000 = 400,000 cm.

Ngayon, sa exam, marami ang madadale sa conversion sa kilometers. Dito papasok ang mental trick: “centi-kilo, 100k!” Bakit? Kasi 1 km = 100,000 cm. Divide 400,000 ÷ 100,000 = 4 km. Kung nakuha mo ang 2, 3, o 5, malamang maling conversion factor ginamit. Kaya tandaan:...
